summary: Fresh independent bounded review of Crosswalk comparison and Plan urgency in the dirty checkout based on 9755c01873444647c30821ac1d0b88aa16023632 found two supported issues: inconsistent overdue semantics for legacy timestamps and loss of keyboard focus during uncached comparison selections. All eight supplied source hashes matched at entry and completion; no worker conclusions were read.

findings.mechanism: Legacy dueDate timestamps are rounded down to a UTC day and Plan waits until the following midnight before marking them overdue. Existing canonical status logic preserves timestamp precision. Therefore a task whose timestamp deadline passed earlier today appears as Due today, below review work, even while Overview attention and linked requirement status treat it as overdue. This changes urgency for retained legacy records by up to almost a day.
findings.evidence: Executed Node import reproduction on the reviewed source: dueDate=2026-10-13T12:00:00Z and at=2026-10-13T18:00:00Z yielded coreOverdue:true, planOverdue:false, planUrgency:{rank:3,label:"Due today",tone:"review"}. apps/server/src/services/visua.ts:301-305 explicitly permits unedited old records to retain timestamps; attention.ts:133 and views.ts:248 consume canonical isTaskOverdue. The existing Plan unit suite passes but does not check this canonical agreement.
findings.recommendation: Use the canonical overdue semantics for Plan: date-only deadlines stay due through the UTC day, while timezone-qualified legacy timestamps retain their recorded instant. Keep UTC-day projection for timeline display. Add a focused regression comparing both calculations before/after a legacy timestamp deadline and ensure an open Plan refreshes when that deadline passes.

findings.mechanism: Selecting an uncached cell/group, page or evidence artifact changes the query key. With no placeholder data, result.data becomes undefined, so the loading-only return removes the complete matrix and its focused control. When the response arrives all controls are recreated without focus restoration. A keyboard user loses their current matrix or pagination position on each first-time selection and has to traverse the view again; an announced loading message does not preserve focus.
findings.evidence: Source trace: queryKey includes the full comparison query at line 19; the cell/group/page/evidence handlers update query parameters; line 37 returns only a heading and loading status while the new key has no data. No retained control shell, focus ref, autofocus, or completion focus effect exists in this component. The app query defaults in main.tsx provide no placeholder data. This is a supported source-derived failure path; no browser reproduction was run because the lead owns that lane.
findings.recommendation: Keep the interactive control shell stable during comparison loads or restore focus by logical control identity after results arrive. Preserve the rule against presenting old pair/detail data. Verify keyboard selection of an uncached cell, pagination and evidence selection, including a deliberately delayed response.

limitations: No browser/build/server/full-suite/production operations were run; those lanes belong to the lead. Visual rendering, touch behavior and the focus-loss path were reviewed from source, not newly observed in a browser.
Targeted server verification covered SQLite in memory only, not PostgreSQL. Test execution does not establish untested concurrency or malformed persisted-record behavior.
The review is bound to the eight supplied hashes and the inspected dependencies at review time; subsequent fixes require affected-path verification.
